newsitem.title: UK: Barclays staff reject strike in ballot.
newsitem.headline: Barclays staff reject strike in ballot.

text.p: Staff at Barclays Bank belonging to the union UNiFI have rejected strike action in a ballot announced on Thursday.
UNiFI, which represents two-thirds of the bank's staff said only 46 percent of members voted in favour of strike action but that 67 percent had supported "industrial action" short of a strike.

UNiFI said its executive will meet later on Thursday to decide which action to take. UNiFI and finance workers' union BIFU balloted around 40,000 Barclays staff for strike action over proposals which they say could leave over 25,000 staff facing a wage freeze and adversely affect pension expectations.

Barclays urged staff to vote against strike action, accusing the unions of ignoring the views of the "silent majority" and estimating that only one in six members of Barclays staff voted in favour of holding the strike ballot.
Barclays has warned that staff who take industrial action will be in breach of their contracts and said union claims it is instigating a pay and pensions freeze were "simply untrue".

The unions, which together represent more than three quarters of all Barclays staff, oppose what they call Barclays' plan to impose a new pay and grading structure based on performance which will result in a pay and pensions freeze for over half of staff.

Barclays denied its plan will produce a pay freeze but has conceded that staff whose pay is at the top of a particular salary band would not get a pay rise regardless of whether they exceeded their agreed performance plan.
